Winter Solstice Spice Cakes

Served at: Winter Solstice (Yule)

Makes 12 standard muffins/cakesPrep 20 minCook 18-22 min

These warm, spiced cakes are a delightful treat for the Winter Solstice, a time when we celebrate the longest night and the return of the sun's light. Infused with comforting winter spices, dried fruits, and citrus, they symbolize warmth and abundance during the darkest days, perfect for sharing with loved ones around a Yule fire.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (180 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon (2 g) ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon (1 g) ground nutmeg
  • 1/2 teaspoon (1 g) ground ginger
  • 1/4 teaspoon (0.5 g) ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.5 g) salt
  • 3/4 cup (180 ml) whole milk
  • 1 large egg
  • 1/4 cup (56 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) vanilla extract
  • 1 teaspoon orange zest (from about 1/2 orange)
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) dried cranberries or chopped raisins
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) chopped walnuts or pecans (optional)
  • For the Glaze (optional):
  • 1 cup (120 g) powdered sugar
  • 2-3 tablespoons (30-45 ml) fresh orange juice

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or grease it well.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and salt until well combined.
  3. In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the milk, egg, melted butter, vanilla extract, and orange zest.
  4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Stir gently with a spatula until just combined. Do not overmix; a few lumps are fine.
  5. Gently fold in the dried cranberries (and nuts, if using) until evenly distributed.
  6. Divide the batter evenly among the 12 muffin cups, filling each about two-thirds full.
  7. Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center of a cake comes out clean.
  8. Let the cakes cool in the muffin tin for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
  9. If making the glaze: In a small bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar and orange juice until smooth. Drizzle the glaze over the cooled cakes before serving.

Tips

  • For extra richness, substitute half of the milk with buttermilk.
  • These cakes can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days, or frozen for up to 3 months.
  • Consider adding a pinch of cardamom for an even more exotic winter spice blend.
